notes:
Lead inbound from blog post + product hunt. Self-serve sign-up last week, small test app in staging. Primary contact: CTO (Nina Park) + growth PM (Samir Rao). Key convo points:
- Use case: chat-based support agent + vector search of KB (embedding store). Peak spikes expected during product launches (up to ~150-200 rps for short windows). Typical steady-state 10-20 rps.
- Concern: 429s during flash spikes — wants predictable behavior for self-serve customers. "We don't want customers to see errors during marketing bursts, but we also can't eat huge cost."
- Requirements: per-API-key rate limits, burst buckets, documented retry/backoff guidance, ability to set soft quotas with emailed alerts. Prefer hosted API (fast onboarding).
- Model strategy: prefer small/quantized open models for cost control; acceptable to route to cheaper model variant when under heavy load (auto-fallback).
- Latency targets: p50 <200ms, p95 <500ms for chat. Able to tolerate slightly higher p95 during short bursts if not dropping requests.
- Security: SSO for admin console later; basic audit logs now. Data residency not required (NA customers).
- Cost sensitivity: high. Want examples of unit economics and an estimate for 200-rps 30s burst.
- Quote from CTO: "We need clear contract on what happens when we hit the ceiling — throttled 429s, queueing, or graceful downgrades?"
- Internal scope: growth/ops running spike tests this week, will provide traffic traces (JMeter + small Playwright harness).
- Interested in Redwood's Optimize recommendations (batching/caching) to reduce token costs for embeddings and chat history.
